rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes continuous creep loading at elevated temperature and constant stress, whereas the paper varied the modulation period (λ) of multilayer coatings and tested them via room-temperature nanoindentation creep. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies sustained stress at moderate-to-high temperature where diffusion is not dominant, while the paper used room-temperature nanoindentation with varying loading rates and a hold segment. The regimes are contradictory.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes strain partitioning, BCC barriers, and dynamic twinning in the FCC phase to enhance work hardening. The paper's mechanism relies on semicoherent interfaces blocking dislocations, causing pileup and stress-induced interfacial amorphization that enables diffusion/interface-slip creep. These are different mechanisms.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts lower creep rate and higher work hardening for a dual-phase coating versus a single-phase FCC baseline. The paper predicts and finds the greatest creep resistance and a transition to diffusion/interface-slip creep for the semicoherent (λ=16 nm) multilayer compared to coherent-interface or grain-boundary-dominated multilayers.
